messages:
Maria (PM): quick sync — we need to re-prioritize the private deploy roadmap after last week's field calls. major asks: IP preservation for tenant workloads, more graceful upgrade paths (zero/minimal downtime), and an offline installer that works with enterprise package managers. who has bandwidth to scope tradeoffs this sprint?
Alex (EngPlatform): I can take the upgrade path scoping. rough idea: two lanes — in-place rolling upgrades w/ canary + blue/green for major kernel/container changes. need to quantify downtime windows per OS.
Rachael (Field): +1 on IP preservation. customers with stateful peering can't change IPs. they want a tenant-network-mode where we don't SNAT egress. currently we do automatic SNAT on host NAT.
Owen (Solutions): From a sales/ops POV, we need clear compatibility matrix: supported OSes, required kernel modules, and minimum CNI versions. also capture customer-managed routing expectations (static routes vs BGP).
Jordan (Security): any change to network behavior needs a short security review. non-SNAT mode increases attack surface of tenant IPs — we need policy guardrails, e.g., default deny host egress and mandatory subnet isolation.
Sam (EngRuntime): Tech constraints: our current installer applies a host-level NAT rule during bootstrap. Supporting non-SNAT means plumbing a mode into the runtime and adding prefix caching fallbacks for KV cache keying. Feels doable but requires an e2e test matrix.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: private-deploy/edge-installer-v0.9 -> production (canary) at 2025-06-12T22:00Z :rocket:
Alex (EngPlatform): For upgrade choreography, propose the following minimal plan: 1) preflight + ip/route validation 2) drain workloads (graceful) 3) rolling package upgrade 4) post-checks for IP/peering. Add a fallback path to pin previous package version if health checks fail.
Maria (PM): Nice. Rachael, can you assemble 3 customer examples where IP preservation is a hard requirement? add details: peering type (static/BGP), expected downtime tolerance, and desired control plane (our managed handshake vs customer-owned).
Rachael (Field): On it. I have 2 already (Fintech customer + Healthcare lab). will add the third and upload configs.
Owen (Solutions): Question: do we surface a simple toggle (SNAT on/off) or a network-mode selector (host-nat / tenant-preserve / routed)? toggle seems simpler but less expressive.
Jordan (Security): network-mode selector but with strict defaults and an approval workflow for tenant-preserve. Need audit logging + KMS-backed keying for control-plane RPCs.
Sam (EngRuntime): Implementation notes: network-mode selector in installer config (yaml), runtime reads config and selects NAT behavior, and we add a compatibility flag for older controller versions. Example snippet:```yaml
network_mode: tenant-preserve
upgrade_strategy: rolling
```
Alex (EngPlatform): We should estimate effort: scoping (this sprint), prototype (next), e2e tests + field pilot (sprint after). Risk: customers on older Linux distros may lack required iproute2 features — we should tier-support and list unsupported OS versions.
Maria (PM): OK action items: Alex scope upgrade-choreography (this sprint) // Sam prototype change to runtime + installer flags (next) // Rachael collect customer configs (ASAP) // Jordan write security checklist for non-SNAT modes (this sprint) // Owen draft compatibility matrix template. I'll consolidate into a roadmap slice and propose launch gates (pilot -> GA).
Owen (Solutions): I'll start the compatibility template and include fallback notes for IP-preserve -> SNAT rollback.
Rachael (Field): FYI one customer insists on single-digit-second failover window for peering. that may push us to blue/green for that account.
Alex (EngPlatform): noted. we should map customers to default upgrade lane.
Maria (PM): Thanks all. we'll discuss timelines in tomorrow's product standup at 10:30. please add anything missing here. :thumbsup:
